programme.title: Geamaichean a' Cho-fhlaitheis Glaschu 2026/Commonwealth Games Glasgow 2026
programme.desc: Spòrs beò agus geàrr-chunntasan an latha bho Glaschu 2026. Air a lìbhrigeadh le Derek ‘Pluto’ Moireach agus sgioba aithris BBC ALBA. Live sporting action and highlights from Glasgow 2026. Presented by Derek ‘Pluto’ Murray and BBC ALBA’s commentary team.

programme.title: Hoolie
programme.desc: An oidhche as motha de cheòl traidiseanta ann an Alba, tha Hoolie 2024 a’ comharrachadh 100 bliadhna de cheòl Albannach, le rionnagan bho na còmhlain as soirbheachail san dùthaich a’ gabhail chun an àrd-ùrlair. Iad uile le na clachan-mìle aca fhèin, tha Capercaillie, Skerryvore, Mànran, RURA is Talisk a’ comharrachadh linn de cheòl traidiseanta na h-Alba, le cruinneachadh de shàr-luchd-ciùil eile. Scotland’s biggest night of traditional music as Hoolie 2024 commemorates 100 years of Scottish music, featuring a star-studded line-up of some of the most successful bands in the country. Each marking their own milestone year, Capercaillie, Skerryvore, Mànran, RURA and Talisk celebrate a combined century of Scottish traditional music with an array of special guests.

programme.title: Belladrum
programme.desc: Tha Fiona NicChoinnich is Niall Iain Dòmhnallach a’ cur fàilt’ oirbh chun a’ chiad latha aig Belladrum 2025. Anns a’ phrògram seo, bidh an seinneadair cliùiteach Paul Heaton, a bha soirbheachail mar phrìomh sheinneadair dhen bhuidheann indie rock bho na 80an, The Housemartins. Cuide ri Paul air Àrd-Ùrlar Hot House tha Rianne Downey aige air aoigheachd, airson an oidhche a thoirt gu ceann. Fiona MacKenzie and Niall Iain Macdonald welcome you to the first day at Belladrum 2025. This programme features renowned singer Paul Heaton, who was successful as the lead singer of 80s indie rock group The Housemartins. Joining Paul on the Hot House Stage to bring the night to a close is special guest Rianne Downey.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Scene by Scene
programme.desc: Rod Steiger talks to Mark Cousins about his celebrated roles in On the Waterfront, Dr Zhivago and In the Heat of the Night, and shares anecdotes about James Dean, Marilyn Monroe and Elizabeth Taylor.

programme.title: Walking With...
programme.desc: Comedian and author Shappi Khorsandi walks through stunning scenery in the Peak District and along the Monsal Trail. From the hills above Tideswell, Shappi follows tracks and footpaths along Tideswell Dale and Miller’s Dale before reaching the disused railway line of the Monsal Trail. Along the way she meets residents who are charmed by her characteristic wit and ease. Taking time to appreciate the hills and ridges surrounding her, Shappi enjoys a sense of calm and composure in the country air. Walking along the trail as it tunnels through hillsides and over gorges, Shappi takes the opportunity to ‘allow the hills to hold’ her. She talks candidly about her outlook on life and love. Funny and poignant, the comedian speaks of relationships, motherhood and mental health with a refreshing honesty.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: At the former Midlothian mining village of Newtongrange, Michael meets the son of a miner whose name loomed large in the disputes of the 1970s and 1980s, 'Red' Mick McGahey. On the outskirts of Edinburgh, at a recording studio in South Gyle, Michael is transported back to the wild world of 1970s pop with Bay City Rollers guitarist Stuart 'Woody' Wood. Michael leaves Edinburgh and takes the train north to Dalmeny for Queensferry, on the banks of the Firth of Forth. At the Progress Rail foundry, he marvels at the traditional skills still required to produce complex sets of rails for modern tracks in Britain and across the world. On the south bank of the Firth of Forth, Michael recalls the construction during the 1950s and 1960s of the Forth Road Bridge, which he saw as a child from the train window while crossing the rail bridge.

On the south bank of the Firth of Forth, Michael recalls the construction during the 1950s and 1960s of the Forth Road Bridge, which he saw as a child from the train window while crossing the rail bridge.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: The Trump administration has issued subpoenas to several New York Times journalists following reporting about alleged security concerns involving President Trump's new Air Force One, a plane donated by Qatar. The case has prompted debate over the balance between protecting national security and safeguarding press freedom. Claire Atkinson, founder of The Media Mix newsletter, outlines the latest developments. The BBC's latest annual report comes as the corporation warns that public service media is facing a period of jeopardy. The figures show a further fall in licence fee-paying households, alongside changing audience habits and continued financial pressures as charter renewal negotiations continue. Rhodri Talfan Davies, the BBC's deputy director-general, sets out the corporation's position. Broadcaster and author Iain Dale reflects on a career spanning politics, publishing, blogging and radio following the publication of his memoir Have I Said Too Much?. The interview covers the enduring appeal of the radio phone-in, the influence of social media on broadcasting, and changing relationships between politicians and traditional media.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. Young sea lion Rocky takes the biggest step of his life as he leaves the safety of his training area and joins the rest of the colony out on Half Mile Pond. As he finds his place alongside the adult sea lions and the park's newly arrived hippos, the keepers hope months of training will help him adapt to life in the open water. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben revisits the remarkable story of the park's Amur tiger cubs as Ginger and Seeka prepare to leave for new homes, while the team also celebrates 60 years since the safari park first opened its gates, transforming the way people experienced wildlife in Britain. Elsewhere, Megan meets the park's new hippos, Jon devises a new feeding challenge for the Cuban crocodiles, and the lionesses enjoy a very special birthday celebration.

programme.title: The Moment of Proof
programme.desc: West Midlands Police are facing a massive spate of burglaries, and they know one man is responsible for them all. But they just can’t catch him in the act. However quickly police arrive, the intruder seems to have vanished into thin air. The break-ins continue unabated - one of the detectives even gets burgled himself! But a single piece of crucial information from a police informant finally gives officers the upper hand. Also, the National Crime Agency is alerted to a plumber who’s buying gun-making equipment online. Could there be an innocent explanation, or is something unusual going on in his lock-up?

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A skilled voice analyst proves the killer of a missing man is very close to home, and a UK fingerprint expert helps to overturn a miscarriage of justice.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles meets a collector with a thirst for preserving brewery history. In a converted garage in Nottinghamshire, Richard Percival has 1,300 beer trays, dating back more than 100 years. Made of heavy steel with ornate designs, they’re all striking examples of British advertising – and Eric Knowles has arranged a surprise visit for him, to recognise his record-breaking collection! In nearby Newark, two teams hope their items will serve up a profit when they go shopping with their antiques experts. Nick Hall is browsing bargains with the reds, Gary and Ian, and Izzie Balmer is with the blues, Joe and Hazel. With 60 minutes on the clock, the red team spots a pot with a rim made by a well-known silversmith and decide it’s one to think about. Meanwhile, the blues are mixing things up with a pestle and mortar. In Derbyshire, it’s almost time for last orders as auctioneer Charles Hanson gets the bids flowing.

programme.title: Escape to the Country

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: Atlantic bluefin tuna, one of the largest fish in the sea, are making a surprise comeback off Northern Ireland’s coast, sparking an ambitious new vision for local fishing. Davy Frayne and Jonny Thursby, two anglers from the town of Ballycastle, have been fishing for giant bluefin tuna in the area for six years. Now they are attempting to establish a bluefin fishery, boasting catches of up to 1,000 pounds in weight. The stretch between Ballycastle and Rathlin is an unforgiving one, so Davy and Jonny are tested to their limits, fishing in waters where bad weather, strong currents and deep waters can create treacherous conditions. They are on the water at every opportunity, starting at the break of dawn and fishing until the light fades over the water to the west. Ballycastle is a town steeped in fishing history, where the people have longstanding connections with the waters. But in recent years, fleets have diminished and fish stocks have been low. Davy and Jonny are attempting to bring a new form of fishing to this coastline, one never seen before in these waters, and many sceptics doubt the viability of the project.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: Izzie and Robin get rummaging and restoring in York. Could a tractor, a horse and a whole heap of toy cars help a special little girl get the treatment she needs?

programme.title: Granite Harbour

programme.title: Would I Lie to You?
programme.desc: Rob Brydon is back in the host’s chair for the award-winning comedy panel show, with Lee Mack and David Mitchell returning as the lightning-quick team captains. Each week, a stellar cast of celebrity guests reveal extraordinary stories about themselves. But are they telling the truth, or are they making it all up? Sorting the fact from the fiction this week are guest panellists Nabil Abdulrashid, Lucy Beaumont, Gethin Jones and Francesca Mills.

programme.title: Ann Droid
programme.desc: Sue isn’t thrilled that Michael is back with Renee, his cheating wife, and turns down an invite to Renee’s BJJ graduation ceremony, pretending she has other plans and upsetting Michael in the process. Sue doesn’t have any plans, so offers to work in the charity shop to help out Eileen, but it’s a disaster. Sue realises she should go and support Michael after all and prove she’s still a good mum, but Linda causes chaos.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: Atlantic bluefin tuna, one of the largest fish in the sea, are making a surprise comeback off Northern Ireland’s coast, sparking an ambitious new vision for local fishing. Davy Frayne and Jonny Thursby, two anglers from the town of Ballycastle, have been fishing for giant bluefin tuna in the area for six years. Now they are attempting to establish a bluefin fishery, boasting catches of up to 1,000 pounds in weight. The stretch between Ballycastle and Rathlin is an unforgiving one, so Davy and Jonny are tested to their limits, fishing in waters where bad weather, strong currents and deep waters can create treacherous conditions. They are on the water at every opportunity, starting at the break of dawn and fishing until the light fades over the water to the west. Ballycastle is a town steeped in fishing history, where the people have longstanding connections with the waters. But in recent years, fleets have diminished and fish stocks have been low. Davy and Jonny are attempting to bring a new form of fishing to this coastline, one never seen before in these waters, and many sceptics doubt the viability of the project.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. Young sea lion Rocky takes the biggest step of his life as he leaves the safety of his training area and joins the rest of the colony out on Half Mile Pond. As he finds his place alongside the adult sea lions and the park's newly arrived hippos, the keepers hope months of training will help him adapt to life in the open water. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben revisits the remarkable story of the park's Amur tiger cubs as Ginger and Seeka prepare to leave for new homes, while the team also celebrates 60 years since the safari park first opened its gates, transforming the way people experienced wildlife in Britain. Elsewhere, Megan meets the park's new hippos, Jon devises a new feeding challenge for the Cuban crocodiles, and the lionesses enjoy a very special birthday celebration.

programme.title: The Moment of Proof
programme.desc: West Midlands Police are facing a massive spate of burglaries, and they know one man is responsible for them all. But they just can’t catch him in the act. However quickly police arrive, the intruder seems to have vanished into thin air. The break-ins continue unabated - one of the detectives even gets burgled himself! But a single piece of crucial information from a police informant finally gives officers the upper hand. Also, the National Crime Agency is alerted to a plumber who’s buying gun-making equipment online. Could there be an innocent explanation, or is something unusual going on in his lock-up?

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles meets a collector with a thirst for preserving brewery history. Davy Frayne and Jonny Thursby, two anglers from the town of Ballycastle, have been fishing for giant bluefin tuna in the area for six years. Now they are attempting to establish a bluefin fishery, boasting catches of up to 1,000 pounds in weight. The stretch between Ballycastle and Rathlin is an unforgiving one, so Davy and Jonny are tested to their limits, fishing in waters where bad weather, strong currents and deep waters can create treacherous conditions. They are on the water at every opportunity, starting at the break of dawn and fishing until the light fades over the water to the west. Ballycastle is a town steeped in fishing history, where the people have longstanding connections with the waters. But in recent years, fleets have diminished and fish stocks have been low. Davy and Jonny are attempting to bring a new form of fishing to this coastline, one never seen before in these waters, and many sceptics doubt the viability of the project.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: Izzie and Robin get rummaging and restoring in York. Could a tractor, a horse and a whole heap of toy cars help a special little girl get the treatment she needs?

programme.title: Granite Harbour
programme.desc: A birthday celebration ends in tragedy when a girl is found dead near a traveller site. As tensions rise, Lindo and the team uncover secrets that threaten to tear a community apart.

programme.title: Would I Lie to You?
programme.desc: Rob Brydon is back in the host’s chair for the award-winning comedy panel show, with Lee Mack and David Mitchell returning as the lightning-quick team captains. Each week, a stellar cast of celebrity guests reveal extraordinary stories about themselves. But are they telling the truth, or are they making it all up? Sorting the fact from the fiction this week are guest panellists Nabil Abdulrashid, Lucy Beaumont, Gethin Jones and Francesca Mills.

programme.title: Ann Droid
programme.desc: Sue isn’t thrilled that Michael is back with Renee, his cheating wife, and turns down an invite to Renee’s BJJ graduation ceremony, pretending she has other plans and upsetting Michael in the process. Sue doesn’t have any plans, so offers to work in the charity shop to help out Eileen, but it’s a disaster. Sue realises she should go and support Michael after all and prove she’s still a good mum, but Linda causes chaos.

programme.title: Austin
programme.desc: Austin’s rock star persona spirals, Mel faces scrutiny over her sex life, and Ingrid discovers who’s secretly writing Big Bear.

programme.title: Austin
programme.desc: After appearing on a controversial podcast and getting Haley fired, Austin faces a family intervention. Meanwhile, Ingrid is auditioning the whole of Canberra to find an actor to play Big Bear before she loses the show. The last audition, a late entry, may be the one.

programme.title: La La Land
programme.desc: Mia (Emma Stone), an aspiring actress, and Sebastian (Ryan Gosling), a dedicated jazz musician, fall in love while struggling to make ends meet in a city known for crushing hopes and breaking hearts. Set in modern-day Los Angeles, this award-winning musical about everyday life explores the joy and pain of pursuing your dreams.

programme.title: Alan Carr's Picture Slam
programme.desc: Comedian Alan Carr returns to host the fun and frantic quiz show where every question is a picture and every picture is worth cash. They could be anything from famous faces, places, products or logos, and teams need to name them all for a Picture Slam. Playing this time are friends Selin and Harin from London, cousins Gerard and Jeremy from South Wales and Kev and Bex, a couple from Motherwell. They battle it out across four rounds, shouting out answers and building their banks. But only one team can make it to the final Super Slam for the chance to win £10,000.

programme.title: Joins BBC News
programme.desc: BBC One joins the BBC's rolling news channel for a night of news.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. Young sea lion Rocky takes the biggest step of his life as he leaves the safety of his training area and joins the rest of the colony out on Half Mile Pond. As he finds his place alongside the adult sea lions and the park's newly arrived hippos, the keepers hope months of training will help him adapt to life in the open water. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben revisits the remarkable story of the park's Amur tiger cubs as Ginger and Seeka prepare to leave for new homes, while the team also celebrates 60 years since the safari park first opened its gates, transforming the way people experienced wildlife in Britain. Elsewhere, Megan meets the park's new hippos, Jon devises a new feeding challenge for the Cuban crocodiles, and the lionesses enjoy a very special birthday celebration.

programme.title: The Moment of Proof
programme.desc: West Midlands Police are facing a massive spate of burglaries, and they know one man is responsible for them all. But they just can’t catch him in the act. However quickly police arrive, the intruder seems to have vanished into thin air. The break-ins continue unabated - one of the detectives even gets burgled himself! But a single piece of crucial information from a police informant finally gives officers the upper hand. Also, the National Crime Agency is alerted to a plumber who’s buying gun-making equipment online. Could there be an innocent explanation, or is something unusual going on in his lock-up?

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A skilled voice analyst proves the killer of a missing man is very close to home, and a UK fingerprint expert helps to overturn a miscarriage of justice.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles meets a collector with a thirst for preserving brewery history. In a converted garage in Nottinghamshire, Richard Percival has 1,300 beer trays, dating back more than 100 years. Made of heavy steel with ornate designs, they’re all striking examples of British advertising – and Eric Knowles has arranged a surprise visit for him, to recognise his record-breaking collection! In nearby Newark, two teams hope their items will serve up a profit when they go shopping with their antiques experts. Nick Hall is browsing bargains with the reds, Gary and Ian, and Izzie Balmer is with the blues, Joe and Hazel. With 60 minutes on the clock, the red team spots a pot with a rim made by a well-known silversmith and decide it’s one to think about. Meanwhile, the blues are mixing things up with a pestle and mortar. In Derbyshire, it’s almost time for last orders as auctioneer Charles Hanson gets the bids flowing.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Australia

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A couple want to swap their Cheshire townhouse for the dark skies and beautiful open spaces of Shropshire. Denise Nurse helps them with the property search and also visits a flower farm in full bloom to witness at first hand how modern technology is working hand-in-hand with nature.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: Izzie and Saf clear a bungalow of quirky collectibles, including an Egyptian sarcophagus and a suffragette mannequin. However, they lose track of the time during a cuckoo clock fix.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles meets a collector with a thirst for preserving brewery history. In a converted garage in Nottinghamshire, Richard Percival has 1,300 beer trays, dating back more than 100 years. Made of heavy steel with ornate designs, they’re all striking examples of British advertising – and Eric Knowles has arranged a surprise visit for him, to recognise his record-breaking collection! In nearby Newark, two teams hope their items will serve up a profit when they go shopping with their antiques experts. Nick Hall is browsing bargains with the reds, Gary and Ian, and Izzie Balmer is with the blues, Joe and Hazel. With 60 minutes on the clock, the red team spots a pot with a rim made by a well-known silversmith and decide it’s one to think about. Meanwhile, the blues are mixing things up with a pestle and mortar. In Derbyshire, it’s almost time for last orders as auctioneer Charles Hanson gets the bids flowing.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: Atlantic bluefin tuna, one of the largest fish in the sea, are making a surprise comeback off Northern Ireland’s coast, sparking an ambitious new vision for local fishing. Davy Frayne and Jonny Thursby, two anglers from the town of Ballycastle, have been fishing for giant bluefin tuna in the area for six years. Now they are attempting to establish a bluefin fishery, boasting catches of up to 1,000 pounds in weight. The stretch between Ballycastle and Rathlin is an unforgiving one, so Davy and Jonny are tested to their limits, fishing in waters where bad weather, strong currents and deep waters can create treacherous conditions. They are on the water at every opportunity, starting at the break of dawn and fishing until the light fades over the water to the west. Ballycastle is a town steeped in fishing history, where the people have longstanding connections with the waters. But in recent years, fleets have diminished and fish stocks have been low. Davy and Jonny are attempting to bring a new form of fishing to this coastline, one never seen before in these waters, and many sceptics doubt the viability of the project.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: Atlantic bluefin tuna, one of the largest fish in the sea, are making a surprise comeback off Northern Ireland’s coast, sparking an ambitious new vision for local fishing. Davy Frayne and Jonny Thursby, two anglers from the town of Ballycastle, have been fishing for giant bluefin tuna in the area for six years. Now they are attempting to establish a bluefin fishery, boasting catches of up to 1,000 pounds in weight. The stretch between Ballycastle and Rathlin is an unforgiving one, so Davy and Jonny are tested to their limits, fishing in waters where bad weather, strong currents and deep waters can create treacherous conditions. They are on the water at every opportunity, starting at the break of dawn and fishing until the light fades over the water to the west. Ballycastle is a town steeped in fishing history, where the people have longstanding connections with the waters. But in recent years, fleets have diminished and fish stocks have been low. Davy and Jonny are attempting to bring a new form of fishing to this coastline, one never seen before in these waters, and many sceptics doubt the viability of the project.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. Young sea lion Rocky takes the biggest step of his life as he leaves the safety of his training area and joins the rest of the colony out on Half Mile Pond. As he finds his place alongside the adult sea lions and the park's newly arrived hippos, the keepers hope months of training will help him adapt to life in the open water. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben revisits the remarkable story of the park's Amur tiger cubs as Ginger and Seeka prepare to leave for new homes, while the team also celebrates 60 years since the safari park first opened its gates, transforming the way people experienced wildlife in Britain. Elsewhere, Megan meets the park's new hippos, Jon devises a new feeding challenge for the Cuban crocodiles, and the lionesses enjoy a very special birthday celebration.

programme.title: The Moment of Proof
programme.desc: West Midlands Police are facing a massive spate of burglaries, and they know one man is responsible for them all. But they just can’t catch him in the act. However quickly police arrive, the intruder seems to have vanished into thin air. The break-ins continue unabated - one of the detectives even gets burgled himself! But a single piece of crucial information from a police informant finally gives officers the upper hand. Also, the National Crime Agency is alerted to a plumber who’s buying gun-making equipment online. Could there be an innocent explanation, or is something unusual going on in his lock-up?

However quickly police arrive, the intruder seems to have vanished into thin air. The break-ins continue unabated - one of the detectives even gets burgled himself! But a single piece of crucial information from a police informant finally gives officers the upper hand. Also, the National Crime Agency is alerted to a plumber who’s buying gun-making equipment online. Could there be an innocent explanation, or is something unusual going on in his lock-up?

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A skilled voice analyst proves the killer of a missing man is very close to home, and a UK fingerprint expert helps to overturn a miscarriage of justice.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles meets a collector with a thirst for preserving brewery history. In a converted garage in Nottinghamshire, Richard Percival has 1,300 beer trays, dating back more than 100 years. Made of heavy steel with ornate designs, they’re all striking examples of British advertising – and Eric Knowles has arranged a surprise visit for him, to recognise his record-breaking collection! In nearby Newark, two teams hope their items will serve up a profit when they go shopping with their antiques experts. Nick Hall is browsing bargains with the reds, Gary and Ian, and Izzie Balmer is with the blues, Joe and Hazel. With 60 minutes on the clock, the red team spots a pot with a rim made by a well-known silversmith and decide it’s one to think about. Meanwhile, the blues are mixing things up with a pestle and mortar. In Derbyshire, it’s almost time for last orders as auctioneer Charles Hanson gets the bids flowing.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: Atlantic bluefin tuna, one of the largest fish in the sea, are making a surprise comeback off Northern Ireland’s coast, sparking an ambitious new vision for local fishing. Davy Frayne and Jonny Thursby, two anglers from the town of Ballycastle, have been fishing for giant bluefin tuna in the area for six years. Now they are attempting to establish a bluefin fishery, boasting catches of up to 1,000 pounds in weight. The stretch between Ballycastle and Rathlin is an unforgiving one, so Davy and Jonny are tested to their limits, fishing in waters where bad weather, strong currents and deep waters can create treacherous conditions. They are on the water at every opportunity, starting at the break of dawn and fishing until the light fades over the water to the west. Ballycastle is a town steeped in fishing history, where the people have longstanding connections with the waters. But in recent years, fleets have diminished and fish stocks have been low. Davy and Jonny are attempting to bring a new form of fishing to this coastline, one never seen before in these waters, and many sceptics doubt the viability of the project.

programme.title: Would I Lie to You?

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. Young sea lion Rocky takes the biggest step of his life as he leaves the safety of his training area and joins the rest of the colony out on Half Mile Pond. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben revisits the remarkable story of the park's Amur tiger cubs as Ginger and Seeka prepare to leave for new homes, while the team also celebrates 60 years since the safari park first opened its gates, transforming the way people experienced wildlife in Britain. Elsewhere, Megan meets the park's new hippos, Jon devises a new feeding challenge for the Cuban crocodiles, and the lionesses enjoy a very special birthday celebration.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: Atlantic bluefin tuna, one of the largest fish in the sea, are making a surprise comeback off Northern Ireland’s coast, sparking an ambitious new vision for local fishing. Davy Frayne and Jonny Thursby, two anglers from the town of Ballycastle, have been fishing for giant bluefin tuna in the area for six years. Now they are attempting to establish a bluefin fishery, boasting catches of up to 1,000 pounds in weight. The stretch between Ballycastle and Rathlin is an unforgiving one, so Davy and Jonny are tested to their limits, fishing in waters where bad weather, strong currents and deep waters can create treacherous conditions. They are on the water at every opportunity, starting at the break of dawn and fishing until the light fades over the water to the west. Ballycastle is a town steeped in fishing history, where the people have longstanding connections with the waters. But in recent years, fleets have diminished and fish stocks have been low. Davy and Jonny are attempting to bring a new form of fishing to this coastline, one never seen before in these waters, and many sceptics doubt the viability of the project.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles meets a collector with a thirst for preserving brewery history. In a converted garage in Nottinghamshire, Richard Percival has 1,300 beer trays, dating back more than 100 years. Made of heavy steel with ornate designs, they’re all striking examples of British advertising – and Eric Knowles has arranged a surprise visit for him, to recognise his record-breaking collection! In nearby Newark, two teams hope their items will serve up a profit when they go shopping with their antiques experts. Nick Hall is browsing bargains with the reds, Gary and Ian, and Izzie Balmer is with the blues, Joe and Hazel. With 60 minutes on the clock, the red team spots a pot with a rim made by a well-known silversmith and decide it’s one to think about. Meanwhile, the blues are mixing things up with a pestle and mortar. In Derbyshire, it’s almost time for last orders as auctioneer Charles Hanson gets the bids flowing.

Elsewhere, Megan meets the park's new hippos, Jon devises a new feeding challenge for the Cuban crocodiles, and the lionesses enjoy a very special birthday celebration.

programme.title: The Moment of Proof
programme.desc: West Midlands Police are facing a massive spate of burglaries, and they know one man is responsible for them all. But they just can’t catch him in the act. However quickly police arrive, the intruder seems to have vanished into thin air. The break-ins continue unabated - one of the detectives even gets burgled himself! But a single piece of crucial information from a police informant finally gives officers the upper hand. Also, the National Crime Agency is alerted to a plumber who’s buying gun-making equipment online. Could there be an innocent explanation, or is something unusual going on in his lock-up?

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles meets a collector with a thirst for preserving brewery history. In a converted garage in Nottinghamshire, Richard Percival has 1,300 beer trays, dating back more than 100 years. Made of heavy steel with ornate designs, they’re all striking examples of British advertising – and Eric Knowles has arranged a surprise visit for him, to recognise his record-breaking collection! In nearby Newark, two teams hope their items will serve up a profit when they go shopping with their antiques experts. Nick Hall is browsing bargains with the reds, Gary and Ian, and Izzie Balmer is with the blues, Joe and Hazel. Meanwhile, the blues are mixing things up with a pestle and mortar. In Derbyshire, it’s almost time for last orders as auctioneer Charles Hanson gets the bids flowing.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: Atlantic bluefin tuna, one of the largest fish in the sea, are making a surprise comeback off Northern Ireland’s coast, sparking an ambitious new vision for local fishing. Davy Frayne and Jonny Thursby, two anglers from the town of Ballycastle, have been fishing for giant bluefin tuna in the area for six years. Now they are attempting to establish a bluefin fishery, boasting catches of up to 1,000 pounds in weight. The stretch between Ballycastle and Rathlin is an unforgiving one, so Davy and Jonny are tested to their limits, fishing in waters where bad weather, strong currents and deep waters can create treacherous conditions. They are on the water at every opportunity, starting at the break of dawn and fishing until the light fades over the water to the west. Ballycastle is a town steeped in fishing history, where the people have longstanding connections with the waters. But in recent years, fleets have diminished and fish stocks have been low. Davy and Jonny are attempting to bring a new form of fishing to this coastline, one never seen before in these waters, and many sceptics doubt the viability of the project.

programme.title: Scotland's Greatest Escape
programme.desc: JJ Chalmers and Grado uncover the best holiday escapes in Scotland. But it’s up to friends and families from all over Scotland to decide which escapes make it to the grand final. Scotland's greatest mind, body and soul escape is decided by father and daughter Graham and Aimee from Dumfriesshire. They jump out of their city break comfort zone into three well-being retreats, as they are soothed by the elegant Stobo spa, experience a close encounter at Sheepy Sleepovers and enjoy a handcrafted Romani caravan at Roulotte Retreat.

programme.title: Paramedics on Scene
programme.desc: Paramedics are mobilised to a large building fire in Glasgow City Centre, with concerns that people are trapped inside. As a PRU - or Paramedic Response Unit - Stewart is often deployed to some of the ambulance service’s most urgent emergencies. As fire and rescue battle the blaze, Stewart endures heavy rain and prepares to treat casualties. Meanwhile, Ayr-based crew Sophie and Shelby treat a man who has been drinking alcohol and gotten injured in a fall. He has sustained a concerning head injury but is adamant he doesn’t want to go to hospital. For Sophie and Shelby, who want to take the patient to a place of safety, it’s a frustrating situation that is one of around 20,000 alcohol-related calls that the ambulance service attends every year. In Glasgow’s Ambulance Control Centre, Fraser takes a difficult 999 call from a woman who is threatening to harm herself following the breakdown of her relationship. Fraser is able to draw on his own mental health experiences to help comfort the caller while further help is arranged. And in Perth, teammates Keara and Ashleigh help Keith, who is undergoing cancer treatment and showing worrying signs of an infection.

programme.title: Ooh the Banter
programme.desc: Jack Docherty brings together a jam-packed cast of comedians, actors and famous faces for a riotous celebration of Scotland's most valuable export – its sense of humour. Scotland is a small nation with a big funny bone. It's known the world over for self-deprecation, quick-witted patter and deadpan asides. But what makes it so funny? To find out the answer, this programme delves deep into the BBC Scotland archives to find a century’s worth of classic characters, catchphrases and comedy clips. A line is drawn from the early days of Scottish comedy on TV from the McFlannels, Stanley Baxter and Lex McLean through to the modern generation of quickfire online sensations. The medium may have changed, but the essence of the humour remains the same - colourful language, authenticity, irreverence and flair for creative insults. Joining Jack will be some of Scotland’s most iconic comedy talent such as Elaine C Smith, Alex Norton, Karen Dunbar, Lawrence Chaney, Brian Cox, Alan Cumming and Forbes Masson.

programme.title: Still Game
programme.desc: Sitcom featuring Jack and Victor, two irrepressible pensioners first seen in the comedy series Chewin' the Fat, along with their dependable pals Winston and Tam, fresh out of Craiglang and taking on the world. Jack and Victor are worried that old Bert has gone downhill since his wife died. Meanwhile Winston has acquired a limp and a home help. Could romance be on the cards?

programme.title: Two Doors Down
programme.desc: Michelle forces Alan to share his family box of doughnuts with the neighbours. Over at Beth and Eric’s, everyone is tucking into the sticky stuff when the new neighbours turn up at the door. Ash and Iqbal are welcomed with awkward stories about the previous owners and the local amenities, though it’s when they reveal they work for the NHS that Ash and Iqbal really grab the neighbours’ attention. But Iqbal isn’t the right kind of doctor for Christine, and Ash reveals they don’t eat takeaways, leaving everyone dumbfounded. Will it be happy ever after in Latimer Crescent for Ash and Iqbal?

programme.title: Rip It Up
programme.desc: Series looking at Scotland's pop music. Here, the biggest names in Scotland's early pop, such as Lulu or The Skids, tell their unique tales in their own words.

programme.title: Hunting the Rolex Rippers
programme.desc: More and more luxury watches are being snatched off UK streets. In 2022, there was an estimated 60 per cent increase in watch thefts worldwide. It is now the crime of choice for many criminals, seen as easier and more lucrative than drug dealing. In this documentary, journalist Tir Dhondy gets access, for the first time ever, to the gang members behind the crime. She meets the teenage moped riders snatching watches off the street, as well as a gang leader who runs a team of teenage watch rippers and female watch spotters. Tir also comes face-to-face with the 16-year-old who used a machete to steal singer Aled Jones’s £17,000 Rolex in broad daylight.

programme.title: Sin City: The Real Las Vegas
programme.desc: Las Vegas has reinvented itself to pull in a new generation of visitors - recasting the city away from being the home of gambling to the world’s go-to destination for live entertainment. In this two-part series, reporter Tir Dhondy finds out how the city has changed, what this new improved version of Vegas offers today’s visitors, and how this shift is being felt by the people who live and work there.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall and the Deadly crew find themselves in deep water as they head into the flooded forests of Brazil. The water is teeming with life and Steve takes a swim in a piranha-infested river in order to find out more about these killer fish. They are assured of a place on the Deadly 60 list until other mysterious fish lurking in the depths make Steve think again. Determined to see one of the strangest animals that inhabit the waters of the flooded forest, Steve and the team go in search of pink river dolphins, and an encounter with one of the most venomous snakes on the planet rounds off this flooded forest adventure.

programme.title: Horrible Histories: The Movie
programme.desc: When Roman lad Atti offends edgy Emperor Nero, he is drafted to fight in far-flung Britain, where local Celt lass Orla itches to join Boudicca’s uprising against the occupying legions. Comedy from BBC Films.

programme.title: Ludwig
programme.desc: John and the gang go back to school to investigate the suspicious death of a headmaster. In doing so, John is faced with his own bad memories of school but is pleasantly surprised when he reconnects with his old mentor, the man who taught him everything about puzzles. With John distracted by the case, Lucy follows a new lead which she hopes will bring her closer to finding James. Lucy’s covert mission takes her to Wales, but she’s not the lone wolf she thinks she is, and her discoveries leave her rattled. A shocking revelation from IT consultant Holly forces John to question everything.

programme.title: Fleabag
programme.desc: Angry, pervy, outrageous and hilarious, Fleabag arrives with a bang as she spins through the city grasping at anyone and anything that might keep her head above water.

programme.title: Fleabag
programme.desc: Haunted by memories of her dead best friend, dumped by her emotionally fragile boyfriend and now desperately trying to sell her stolen goods, Fleabag attempts to rekindle romantic fires to distract her from the mayhem of her life.

programme.title: Fleabag
programme.desc: Fleabag helps her inappropriate brother-in-law buy a present for Claire, who is organising her own surprise birthday party. On the hunt for a date, Fleabag reconnects with a toothy friend.

programme.title: Fleabag
programme.desc: Fleabag and her sister Claire reluctantly visit a female-only silent retreat, courtesy of their father. Their enforced silence is interrupted by an unusual neighbouring weekend workshop, explosive secrets coming to light and there is a surprising connection with an old acquaintance.

programme.title: Fleabag
programme.desc: On the anniversary of her mother's death, Fleabag and Claire return to their family home for the annual memorial lunch. Although this time there is an interloper... Things get heated between Fleabag and her godmother, who muscles her way into the occasion and reveals plans for her sex-hibition.

programme.title: Fleabag
programme.desc: Fleabag takes a date to her godmother's Sex-hibition to discover a few shocks are in store for her there, including a declaration of love, a familiar piece of work and an entire wall of surprises. But where is Claire? The season finale forces Fleabag to face up to her actions and to finally reveal what happened to her beloved friend Boo.

programme.title: Hunting the Rolex Rippers
programme.desc: More and more luxury watches are being snatched off UK streets. In 2022, there was an estimated 60 per cent increase in watch thefts worldwide. It is now the crime of choice for many criminals, seen as easier and more lucrative than drug dealing. In this documentary, journalist Tir Dhondy gets access, for the first time ever, to the gang members behind the crime. She meets the teenage moped riders snatching watches off the street, as well as a gang leader who runs a team of teenage watch rippers and female watch spotters. Tir also comes face-to-face with the 16-year-old who used a machete to steal singer Aled Jones’s £17,000 Rolex in broad daylight.

programme.title: Sin City: The Real Las Vegas
programme.desc: Las Vegas has reinvented itself to pull in a new generation of visitors - recasting the city away from being the home of gambling to the world’s go-to destination for live entertainment. In this two-part series, reporter Tir Dhondy finds out how the city has changed, what this new improved version of Vegas offers today’s visitors, and how this shift is being felt by the people who live and work there.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: A helicopter trip over the vast expanse of Brazil's northern savannah helps adventurer Steve Backshall find his next contender for the Deadly 60. He is in search of the elusive giant anteater, but can he get close enough to film one for his list? A chance encounter with a tough little owl with an ingenious way of catching its supper captures Steve's attention and the rainforest lives up to its name as a very wet team ventures out at night looking for some of the world's deadliest bugs.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall and the Deadly crew find themselves in deep water as they head into the flooded forests of Brazil. The water is teeming with life and Steve takes a swim in a piranha-infested river in order to find out more about these killer fish. They are assured of a place on the Deadly 60 list until other mysterious fish lurking in the depths make Steve think again. Determined to see one of the strangest animals that inhabit the waters of the flooded forest, Steve and the team go in search of pink river dolphins, and an encounter with one of the most venomous snakes on the planet rounds off this flooded forest adventure.

programme.title: Horrible Histories: The Movie
programme.desc: When Roman lad Atti offends edgy Emperor Nero, he is drafted to fight in far-flung Britain, where local Celt lass Orla itches to join Boudicca’s uprising against the occupying legions. Comedy from BBC Films.

programme.title: Ludwig
programme.desc: John and the gang go back to school to investigate the suspicious death of a headmaster. In doing so, John is faced with his own bad memories of school but is pleasantly surprised when he reconnects with his old mentor, the man who taught him everything about puzzles. With John distracted by the case, Lucy follows a new lead which she hopes will bring her closer to finding James. Lucy’s covert mission takes her to Wales, but she’s not the lone wolf she thinks she is, and her discoveries leave her rattled. A shocking revelation from IT consultant Holly forces John to question everything.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. It's a milestone moment for the park's young Amur tigers as sisters Ginger Biscuit and Seeka begin preparations to leave home. As part of the international breeding programme, they'll soon move to new collections to help secure the future of one of the world's rarest big cats. But before they can go, the keepers face the challenge of preparing them for life apart and training them to enter their transport crates for the very first time. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate look back at an extraordinary conservation adventure when Longleat keepers travelled to Tanzania to help renowned conservationist Tony Fitzjohn relocate endangered African wild dogs. This remarkable story would go on to influence conservation work back at the park for years to come. Elsewhere, Megan introduces the park's emus to an unusual new treat, while the recently arrived maned wolves begin settling into their new home as keepers learn to tell the three sisters apart.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing Simply Provence
programme.desc: It’s fair to say that when it comes to classic national dishes, the French and British like to do things differently. However, both have a passion for poisson. Forty-five per cent of French households eat fish at least once a week, and Marcus wants to find out what kind of fish they like and if there’s a French dish to rival the great British fish and chips. If there's one fruit that might be even more synonymous with Provence than garlic, it's the olive. They’ve been grown here for over 3,500 years, and Marcus wants to understand the region’s passion for these tiny, versatile delights.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Political Thinking with Nick Robinson
programme.desc: Nick Robinson in conversation with people who influence our political thinking.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Kemah Bob, JJ Chalmers, Kevin Clifton and Victoria Derbyshire take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quick-fire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games kitchen composter?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp hosts this quiz show with sidekick Sarah Greene where contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple - make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Debbie and Paul may not come from farming backgrounds, but Debbie’s determination after quitting her office job means they are now the proud owners of 300 alpacas on their Northumberland farm. They are heading to the Westmorland County Show in Cumbria, hoping to return home with rosettes and maybe even the champion breed title, which they have won before. Meanwhile, Lancashire alpaca farmer Bev also faces the heat of competition, and a champion win would take her one step closer to fulfilling her dream of full-time farming in the future.

programme.title: The Hidden World of Hospitality with Tom Kerridge
programme.desc: The biggest celebrations in people's lives would be nothing without great hospitality operators working tirelessly behind the scenes. Tom looks at how the industry delivers exceptional service on a huge scale. In Wolverhampton, Tom meets the team behind Grand Station, a large events venue housed in a former railway station. In the Scottish village of Grandtully, the Highland Chocolatier supplies the trade with fine chocolates relied upon by the hospitality industry. And Tom has a huge catering event of his own: the Six Nations rugby match between England and France at Twickenham.

programme.title: Wild Brazil
programme.desc: This intimate journey into the heart of Brazil concludes. A fierce drought ensues, culminating in huge and ferocious fires. The capuchin monkeys, giant otters, coatis and jaguars are proving their extreme survival skills, while looking for mates and racing to breed to ensure that the next generation are born just as the good times arrive again. Astonishing footage tells an extraordinary tale of love in a harsh world.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin presents from Norwich Cathedral in Norfolk. In the great nave, experts Thomas Plant and David Fletcher pick out some choice items to take to auction. Among them are a masonic watch and a much sought-after commemorative mug by Eric Ravilious. Paul also visits the extravagant home of Britain's first prime minister, Robert Walpole.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, four previous players who came close to winning but never quite made it - Fern Britton, JB Gill, John Kearns and Sally Lindsay - take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. With their second chance at winning a prize, will they opt for the House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Just One Thing
programme.desc: In Edinburgh, 70-year-old Alister’s cycling accidents have resulted in a few knocks to his health and his confidence. Roman Kemp has a counterintuitive solution: easy exercise. It sounds backwards, but research shows that 'reverse' moves – like walking downhill instead of up, or lowering weights instead of lifting them – could deliver bigger gains in muscle strength, bone density and blood sugar control. Sometimes, the easy route really is the smart one.

programme.title: Grand Tours of Scotland's Lochs
programme.desc: Paul follows in the footsteps of Bonnie Prince Charlie exploring the lesser-known lochs along the west coast of Scotland. Landing at Glenuig, he makes his way inland to Loch Moidart and MacDonald country, walking the old coffin road, which was used for centuries by funeral parties, taking their dead to a sacred isle. On the track Paul meets a trials bike enthusiast and learns the secrets of a 'dabbing coat' before landing off the Green Isle where he rings a 1,100-year-old bell for the dead. Taking a boat north, Paul sails up Loch Shiel to Glenfinnan where Bonnie Prince Charlie officially began his rising to reclaim the throne for the Stuart dynasty. From a forgotten monument that commemorates this event, Paul heads back to the coast and Loch Ailort, where he learns how to knife fight before taking a trip across the loch to a deserted community on the roadless Ardnish peninsula.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: It's all about the borders at Beechgrove Garden as Brian Cunningham and Kirsty Wilson replant, fill gaps and replace losses all around the plot. Kirsty revisits her hot border, designed to display vibrant colours at the height of summer. The winter temperatures killed off a few plants, so she will be trying out some alternatives. Brian is in the calendar border, created to have some form of colour or interest every month of the year. It has not had much attention this year, so Brian will be topping it up to ensure year-round performance. Kirsty will also be planting in the border behind Beechgrove's main pond, where other gaps have appeared, and she is building a new structure to create a habitat for pollinators. There is a trip to visit a great garden on the Cowal Peninsula, and all the week's handy hints.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: It’s the first ever RHS Sandringham Flower Show, and Arit Anderson, Jamie Butterworth and Frances Tophill are on hand to take a look around. From spectacular show gardens to a floral marquee packed full of horticultural goodies, there is something to whet the appetite. A local grower who knows everything there is to know about roses provides expert advice, while a National Collection holder in Lincolnshire shines a light on drought-tolerant achilleas. A couple in Kent share their new-found love of succulents, with some useful advice on how to care for them. And in Hampshire, a plantsman conveys his passion for carrying on the family tradition of running a nursery.

programme.title: Bergerac
programme.desc: Bergerac is a broken man, battling his demons and on leave after the death of his wife. But when a member of the Wakefields, one of Jersey’s wealthiest families, is murdered, chief of police Uma Dalal wants their best detective on the case. The Wakefields, led by patriarch Arthur, are keeping their cards close to their chests, whilst a man from Bergerac’s past surfaces to make a shocking accusation. Is Bergerac up to the job?

programme.title: Bergerac
programme.desc: The police are desperate to find kidnapped baby Lily before it is too late. Bergerac questions convicted kidnapper John Blakely, and the battle lines are drawn between these two old foes. But Bergerac doesn’t care who he upsets in his quest to find Lily and bring Cate’s killer to justice. Meanwhile, Bergerac disappoints his daughter Kim again and incurs the wrath of his mother-in-law, Charlie Hungerford. But he also uncovers the shocking truth of who kidnapped baby Lily.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Matt Chorley.

programme.title: Janet Planet
programme.desc: Twelve-year-old Lacy is growing up in rural Massachusetts with her loving mother, Janet, in the summer of 1991. About to enter middle school in a few weeks' time, Lacy has a hard time making friends but has a healthy imagination, and she is captivated by her mother and the variety of the few friends her mother brings home.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Criminal gangs are targeting the rental market to take over properties and use them to run their operations. Panorama reporter Hazel Martin speaks to flat owners who paid reputable agencies to do tenancy checks but still ended up handing over their keys to criminals using fake IDs and references. One flat was turned into a drugs factory, another became a brothel, and a third was sublet and ransacked. Even when there appears to be clear evidence of criminal behaviour, gangs are escaping prosecution, and landlords say it can take months to repossess their properties.

From a tiny cell over four billion years ago to one of the planet’s most iconic giants, this is the surprising story of life's most radical transformation.

programme.title: Grand Tours of Scotland's Lochs
programme.desc: Paul follows in the footsteps of Bonnie Prince Charlie exploring the lesser-known lochs along the west coast of Scotland. Landing at Glenuig, he makes his way inland to Loch Moidart and MacDonald country, walking the old coffin road, which was used for centuries by funeral parties, taking their dead to a sacred isle. On the track Paul meets a trials bike enthusiast and learns the secrets of a 'dabbing coat' before landing off the Green Isle where he rings a 1,100-year-old bell for the dead. Taking a boat north, Paul sails up Loch Shiel to Glenfinnan where Bonnie Prince Charlie officially began his rising to reclaim the throne for the Stuart dynasty. From a forgotten monument that commemorates this event, Paul heads back to the coast and Loch Ailort, where he learns how to knife fight before taking a trip across the loch to a deserted community on the roadless Ardnish peninsula.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: It's all about the borders at Beechgrove Garden as Brian Cunningham and Kirsty Wilson replant, fill gaps and replace losses all around the plot. Kirsty revisits her hot border, designed to display vibrant colours at the height of summer. The winter temperatures killed off a few plants, so she will be trying out some alternatives. Brian is in the calendar border, created to have some form of colour or interest every month of the year. It has not had much attention this year, so Brian will be topping it up to ensure year-round performance. Kirsty will also be planting in the border behind Beechgrove's main pond, where other gaps have appeared, and she is building a new structure to create a habitat for pollinators. There is a trip to visit a great garden on the Cowal Peninsula, and all the week's handy hints.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: It’s the first ever RHS Sandringham Flower Show, and Arit Anderson, Jamie Butterworth and Frances Tophill are on hand to take a look around. From spectacular show gardens to a floral marquee packed full of horticultural goodies, there is something to whet the appetite. A local grower who knows everything there is to know about roses provides expert advice, while a National Collection holder in Lincolnshire shines a light on drought-tolerant achilleas. A couple in Kent share their new-found love of succulents, with some useful advice on how to care for them. And in Hampshire, a plantsman conveys his passion for carrying on the family tradition of running a nursery.

programme.title: Bergerac
programme.desc: Bergerac is a broken man, battling his demons and on leave after the death of his wife. But when a member of the Wakefields, one of Jersey’s wealthiest families, is murdered, chief of police Uma Dalal wants their best detective on the case. The Wakefields, led by patriarch Arthur, are keeping their cards close to their chests, whilst a man from Bergerac’s past surfaces to make a shocking accusation. Is Bergerac up to the job?

programme.title: Bergerac
programme.desc: The police are desperate to find kidnapped baby Lily before it is too late. Bergerac questions convicted kidnapper John Blakely, and the battle lines are drawn between these two old foes. But Bergerac doesn’t care who he upsets in his quest to find Lily and bring Cate’s killer to justice. Meanwhile, Bergerac disappoints his daughter Kim again and incurs the wrath of his mother-in-law, Charlie Hungerford. But he also uncovers the shocking truth of who kidnapped baby Lily.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Matt Chorley.

programme.title: Janet Planet
programme.desc: Twelve-year-old Lacy is growing up in rural Massachusetts with her loving mother, Janet, in the summer of 1991. About to enter middle school in a few weeks' time, Lacy has a hard time making friends but has a healthy imagination, and she is captivated by her mother and the variety of the few friends her mother brings home.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Criminal gangs are targeting the rental market to take over properties and use them to run their operations. Panorama reporter Hazel Martin speaks to flat owners who paid reputable agencies to do tenancy checks but still ended up handing over their keys to criminals using fake IDs and references. One flat was turned into a drugs factory, another became a brothel, and a third was sublet and ransacked. Even when there appears to be clear evidence of criminal behaviour, gangs are escaping prosecution, and landlords say it can take months to repossess their properties.

programme.title: Evolution
programme.desc: Chris Packham embarks on an extraordinary journey through deep time to uncover how a creature as vast, complex and charismatic as the elephant came to be. From a tiny cell over four billion years ago to one of the planet’s most iconic giants, this is the surprising story of life's most radical transformation.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. It's a milestone moment for the park's young Amur tigers as sisters Ginger Biscuit and Seeka begin preparations to leave home. As part of the international breeding programme, they'll soon move to new collections to help secure the future of one of the world's rarest big cats. But before they can go, the keepers face the challenge of preparing them for life apart and training them to enter their transport crates for the very first time. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate look back at an extraordinary conservation adventure when Longleat keepers travelled to Tanzania to help renowned conservationist Tony Fitzjohn relocate endangered African wild dogs. This remarkable story would go on to influence conservation work back at the park for years to come. Elsewhere, Megan introduces the park's emus to an unusual new treat, while the recently arrived maned wolves begin settling into their new home as keepers learn to tell the three sisters apart.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.desc: Criminal gangs are targeting the rental market to take over properties and use them to run their operations. Panorama reporter Hazel Martin speaks to flat owners who paid reputable agencies to do tenancy checks but still ended up handing over their keys to criminals using fake IDs and references. One flat was turned into a drugs factory, another became a brothel, and a third was sublet and ransacked. Even when there appears to be clear evidence of criminal behaviour, gangs are escaping prosecution, and landlords say it can take months to repossess their properties.

programme.title: Evolution
programme.desc: Chris Packham embarks on an extraordinary journey through deep time to uncover how a creature as vast, complex and charismatic as the elephant came to be. From a tiny cell over four billion years ago to one of the planet’s most iconic giants, this is the surprising story of life's most radical transformation.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. It's a milestone moment for the park's young Amur tigers as sisters Ginger Biscuit and Seeka begin preparations to leave home. As part of the international breeding programme, they'll soon move to new collections to help secure the future of one of the world's rarest big cats. But before they can go, the keepers face the challenge of preparing them for life apart and training them to enter their transport crates for the very first time. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate look back at an extraordinary conservation adventure when Longleat keepers travelled to Tanzania to help renowned conservationist Tony Fitzjohn relocate endangered African wild dogs. This remarkable story would go on to influence conservation work back at the park for years to come. Elsewhere, Megan introduces the park's emus to an unusual new treat, while the recently arrived maned wolves begin settling into their new home as keepers learn to tell the three sisters apart.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing Simply Provence
programme.desc: It’s fair to say that when it comes to classic national dishes, the French and British like to do things differently. However, both have a passion for poisson. Forty-five per cent of French households eat fish at least once a week, and Marcus wants to find out what kind of fish they like and if there’s a French dish to rival the great British fish and chips. If there's one fruit that might be even more synonymous with Provence than garlic, it's the olive. They’ve been grown here for over 3,500 years, and Marcus wants to understand the region’s passion for these tiny, versatile delights.

programme.title: BBC News
